chunks: You should know that even the smallest hypocrisy is like believing in more than one God, and keeping company of people who follow their desires is the key to obliviousness from religion, and is the seat of Satan. Be on your guard against falsehood because it is contrary to Faith. A truthful person is on the height of salvation and dignity, while the liar is on the edge of ignominy and degradation. Do not be jealous because jealousy eats away Faith just as fire eats away dried wood. Do not bear malice because, it is scraper (of virtues). And know that desires make wit forgetful and make memory oblivious. You should falsify desire because it is a deception, and he who has desires is in deceit.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual dangers of hypocrisy, desires, and excessive hope according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) synthesizes internal spiritual states with external actions, identifying *riya'* (showing off) as a subtle form of *shirk* that corrupts the purity of faith. This passage serves as a practical guide for self-purification (*tazkiyah*), warning that excessive hope (*amal*) acts as a veil over the intellect, leading to negligence in divine remembrance. It underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning one's inner intentions with outward truthfulness to secure salvation.
